Use income growth data `sample_growth_tb` to examine dependence across periods. Growth is the log difference between end-of-period and beginning-of-period incomes.
Select individuals using beginning-of-period income and age conditions for 2014–15, and calculate Spearman rank correlations over the six periods from 2014–15 to 2019–20.
Also use growth in 2014–15 and 2015–16 to calculate a tail dependence measure and cumulative means of growth in the following period after transforming it to nonnegative values. Include zero growth in both analyses.

## 1 Rank correlations of growth rates

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(pins)

# Specify relative paths for the board, figure output directory, and plotting theme.
board <- board_folder("../income_board_replicate")
graph_dir <- "graph"
dir.create(graph_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
source("theme_ipsum_like.R")
theme_set(theme_ipsum())
```

**Setting sample conditions**

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

library(corrr)
library(scattermore)

```

Define `pobs()` to transform growth rates into rank-based pseudo-observations.
Use average ranks for ties and divide by the length of the original vector plus one.
Leave missing values in their original positions.

```{r}
#| label: define-pobs
pobs <- function(x) {
  rank(x, ties.method = "average", na.last = "keep") / (length(x) + 1)
}
```

Load `sample_growth_tb` and calculate age `age` as the beginning year extracted from period label `year` minus the birth year in the first four characters of `birth_date`.
For 2014–15 growth records (`g_15_14`), save the `id` values of individuals with beginning-of-period income `pre_income` of at least 4 million yen and beginning-of-period age 25–60 in `id_tb`.
Use this set of individuals for both rank correlations and tail analyses.
Do not impose additional restrictions based on income or age in other periods, or on industry.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

sample_growth_tb <- board |> pin_read("sample_growth_tb") |> 
  mutate(age = as.numeric(str_c(20, str_sub(year,6,7))) - as.numeric(str_sub(birth_date,1,4))) 

id_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  filter(year == "g_15_14", 
         pre_income >= 4*10^6, 
         age >= 25, age <= 60) |> 
  select(id) |> 
  distinct(id)

```

**Spearman rank correlations across six periods**

Use a common sample with finite growth rates in all six periods from 2014–15 to 2019–20.
Include zero growth, and exclude individuals with `NA`, `NaN`, or positive or negative infinity.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-growth-wide
growth_periods <- c(
  "g_20_19", "g_19_18", "g_18_17",
  "g_17_16", "g_16_15", "g_15_14"
)

growth_wide_tb <- sample_growth_tb |>
  filter(year %in% growth_periods) |>
  select(id, year, growth) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = year, values_from = growth) |>
  inner_join(id_tb, by = "id") |> 
  select(-id) |> 
  filter(if_all(everything(), is.finite))

growth_wide_tb |> correlate(method = "spearman") 

```

## 2 Dependence in the tail

**Data for the two-period tail analysis**

For the selected individuals, retain observations with finite growth rates in both 2014–15 and 2015–16 in `normal_tb`.
Calculate pseudo-observations separately for these two periods.
Do not require finite values in all six periods here; use `normal_tb` for both the tail dependence measure and cumulative means of growth in the following period.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

normal_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = "year", values_from = "growth") |> 
  inner_join(id_tb, by = "id") |> 
  select(g_16_15, g_15_14) |> 
  filter(is.finite(g_16_15), is.finite(g_15_14)) |> 
  mutate(pobs_16_15 = pobs(g_16_15), pobs_15_14 = pobs(g_15_14)) 

```

**Tail dependence measure**

Let $N_q$ be the number of observations whose pseudo-observations exceed threshold $q$ in both periods, and $N$ the analysis sample size. Calculate the tail dependence measure as $N_q/[N(1-q)]$.
Vary $q$ from 0.8 to 0.9995 in increments of 0.0005, save the measure in `tail_tb`, and plot it against $q$.
Set vertical scale limits of 0–0.3 using `ylim()`.

```{r}

tail_tb <- seq(0.8, 0.9995, by = 0.0005) |> 
  map_dfr(~ normal_tb |> 
            filter(pobs_16_15 > .x, pobs_15_14 > .x) |> 
            summarise(criteria = .x,
                      tail_coeff = (n()/nrow(normal_tb))/(1 - .x))
          )

```

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

tail_tb |> 
ggplot(aes(criteria, tail_coeff)) + 
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") + 
  ylim(0, 0.3) + 
  labs(x = expression(q), 
       y = "Tail dependence") 
ggsave(filename = "tail_coeff_income.png", path = graph_dir)

```

**Cumulative mean of nonnegative growth in the following period**

Sort individuals by descending growth in 2014–15, transform growth in the following period (2015–16) to $\max(g_{16,15}, 0)$, and calculate its cumulative mean.
Use 2014–15 growth $t$ on the horizontal axis to examine average nonnegative growth in the following period among individuals who experienced large growth.
Calculate using all of `normal_tb`, restricting only the displayed horizontal range to 0.2–2 and vertical range to 0–0.5.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

normal_tb |> 
  arrange(desc(g_15_14)) |> 
  mutate(
    g_16_15 = if_else(g_16_15 > 0, g_16_15, 0),
    cummean_16_15 = cummean(g_16_15)
  ) |>
ggplot(aes(g_15_14, cummean_16_15)) +  
  geom_scattermore(pointsize = 1.5, color = "steelblue") + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.2, 2), ylim = c(0, 0.5)) + 
  labs(x = "t", 
       y = "Conditional tail expectation") 
ggsave(filename = "cond_tail_expect_g_15_14_transformed_income.png", path = graph_dir)

```
